_note: Stock resources are moved by assigned porters, and distance in levels equals labour time. Placement is therefore permanent: a hydroponics bay twenty levels from the canteen burns porter-hours every day, forever.

methods.name: Stairwell
methods._concurrentNote: null means unlimited — a stairwell takes as many people as you can put on it, which is exactly why it is the fallback that never fails.
methods._note: Free and always available. The cost is paid in worker condition and in congestion at shift change, when everyone is on the stairs at once.

methods.name: Freight elevator
methods._concurrentNote: One car per elevator building. This is what 'limited-cars' actually means, and it is what pushes overflow onto the stairwell — a Shaft with one elevator and a lot to move has people on the stairs whether it likes it or not.
methods._note: The only method that makes a tall Shaft workable, and the one that stops working exactly when the grid is under strain — which is when hauling matters most.

methods.name: Dumbwaiter
methods._note: Cheap and reliable for small, constant flows — rations to a canteen, parts to a workshop. Useless for ore.
